86:   template <typename U, FMT_ENABLE_IF(std::is_integral<U>::value)>
87:   void operator()(U value) {
88:     bool is_signed = type_ == 'd' || type_ == 'i';
89:     using target_type = conditional_t<std::is_same<T, void>::value, U, T>;
90:     if (const_check(sizeof(target_type) <= sizeof(int))) {
91:       // Extra casts are used to silence warnings.
92:       if (is_signed) {
93:         arg_ = detail::make_arg<Context>(
94:             static_cast<int>(static_cast<target_type>(value)));
95:       } else {
96:         using unsigned_type = typename make_unsigned_or_bool<target_type>::type;
97:         arg_ = detail::make_arg<Context>(
98:             static_cast<unsigned>(static_cast<unsigned_type>(value)));

101:       if (is_signed) {
102:         // glibc's printf doesn't sign extend arguments of smaller types:
103:         //   std::printf("%lld", -42);  // prints "4294967254"
104:         // but we don't have to do the same because it's a UB.
105:         arg_ = detail::make_arg<Context>(static_cast<long long>(value));

114:   void operator()(U) {}  // No conversion needed for non-integral types.

418: template <typename OutputIt, typename Char>
419: void basic_printf_context<OutputIt, Char>::parse_flags(format_specs& specs,
420:                                                        const Char*& it,
421:                                                        const Char* end) {
422:   for (; it != end; ++it) {
423:     switch (*it) {
424:     case '-':
425:       specs.align = align::left;
426:       break;
427:     case '+':
428:       specs.sign = sign::plus;
429:       break;
430:     case '0':
431:       specs.fill[0] = '0';
432:       break;
433:     case ' ':
434:       specs.sign = sign::space;
435:       break;
436:     case '#':
437:       specs.alt = true;
438:       break;
439:     default:
440:       return;
441:     }
442:   }
443: }

455: template <typename OutputIt, typename Char>
456: int basic_printf_context<OutputIt, Char>::parse_header(const Char*& it,
457:                                                        const Char* end,
458:                                                        format_specs& specs) {
459:   int arg_index = -1;
460:   char_type c = *it;
461:   if (c >= '0' && c <= '9') {
462:     // Parse an argument index (if followed by '$') or a width possibly
463:     // preceded with '0' flag(s).
464:     detail::error_handler eh;
465:     int value = parse_nonnegative_int(it, end, eh);
466:     if (it != end && *it == '$') {  // value is an argument index
467:       ++it;
468:       arg_index = value;
469:     } else {
470:       if (c == '0') specs.fill[0] = '0';
471:       if (value != 0) {
472:         // Nonzero value means that we parsed width and don't need to
473:         // parse it or flags again, so return now.
474:         specs.width = value;
475:         return arg_index;
476:       }
477:     }
478:   }
479:   parse_flags(specs, it, end);
480:   // Parse width.
481:   if (it != end) {
482:     if (*it >= '0' && *it <= '9') {
483:       detail::error_handler eh;
484:       specs.width = parse_nonnegative_int(it, end, eh);
485:     } else if (*it == '*') {
486:       ++it;
487:       specs.width = static_cast<int>(visit_format_arg(
488:           detail::printf_width_handler<char_type>(specs), get_arg()));
489:     }
490:   }
491:   return arg_index;
492: }

494: template <typename OutputIt, typename Char>
495: template <typename ArgFormatter>
496: OutputIt basic_printf_context<OutputIt, Char>::format() {
497:   auto out = this->out();
498:   const Char* start = parse_ctx_.begin();
499:   const Char* end = parse_ctx_.end();
500:   auto it = start;
501:   while (it != end) {
502:     char_type c = *it++;
503:     if (c != '%') continue;
504:     if (it != end && *it == c) {
505:       out = std::copy(start, it, out);
506:       start = ++it;
507:       continue;
508:     }
509:     out = std::copy(start, it - 1, out);
510: 
511:     format_specs specs;
512:     specs.align = align::right;
513: 
514:     // Parse argument index, flags and width.
515:     int arg_index = parse_header(it, end, specs);
516:     if (arg_index == 0) on_error("argument not found");
517: 
518:     // Parse precision.
519:     if (it != end && *it == '.') {
520:       ++it;
521:       c = it != end ? *it : 0;
522:       if ('0' <= c && c <= '9') {
523:         detail::error_handler eh;
524:         specs.precision = parse_nonnegative_int(it, end, eh);
525:       } else if (c == '*') {
526:         ++it;
527:         specs.precision = static_cast<int>(
528:             visit_format_arg(detail::printf_precision_handler(), get_arg()));
529:       } else {
530:         specs.precision = 0;
531:       }
532:     }
533: 
534:     format_arg arg = get_arg(arg_index);
535:     if (specs.precision >= 0 && arg.type() == detail::type::cstring_type) {
536:       auto str = visit_format_arg(detail::get_cstring<Char>(), arg);
537:       auto str_end = str + specs.precision;
538:       auto nul = std::find(str, str_end, Char());
539:       arg = detail::make_arg<basic_printf_context>(basic_string_view<Char>(
540:           str,
541:           detail::to_unsigned(nul != str_end ? nul - str : specs.precision)));
542:     }
543:     if (specs.alt && visit_format_arg(detail::is_zero_int(), arg))
544:       specs.alt = false;
545:     if (specs.fill[0] == '0') {
546:       if (arg.is_arithmetic())
547:         specs.align = align::numeric;
548:       else
549:         specs.fill[0] = ' ';  // Ignore '0' flag for non-numeric types.
550:     }
551: 
552:     // Parse length and convert the argument to the required type.
553:     c = it != end ? *it++ : 0;
554:     char_type t = it != end ? *it : 0;
555:     using detail::convert_arg;
556:     switch (c) {
557:     case 'h':
558:       if (t == 'h') {
559:         ++it;
560:         t = it != end ? *it : 0;
561:         convert_arg<signed char>(arg, t);
562:       } else {
563:         convert_arg<short>(arg, t);
564:       }
565:       break;
566:     case 'l':
567:       if (t == 'l') {
568:         ++it;
569:         t = it != end ? *it : 0;
570:         convert_arg<long long>(arg, t);
571:       } else {
572:         convert_arg<long>(arg, t);
573:       }
574:       break;
575:     case 'j':
576:       convert_arg<intmax_t>(arg, t);
577:       break;
578:     case 'z':
579:       convert_arg<size_t>(arg, t);
580:       break;
581:     case 't':
582:       convert_arg<std::ptrdiff_t>(arg, t);
583:       break;
584:     case 'L':
585:       // printf produces garbage when 'L' is omitted for long double, no
586:       // need to do the same.
587:       break;
588:     default:
589:       --it;
590:       convert_arg<void>(arg, c);
591:     }
592: 
593:     // Parse type.
594:     if (it == end) FMT_THROW(format_error("invalid format string"));
595:     specs.type = static_cast<char>(*it++);
596:     if (arg.is_integral()) {
597:       // Normalize type.
598:       switch (specs.type) {
599:       case 'i':
600:       case 'u':
601:         specs.type = 'd';
602:         break;
603:       case 'c':
604:         visit_format_arg(detail::char_converter<basic_printf_context>(arg),
605:                          arg);
606:         break;
607:       }
608:     }
609: 
610:     start = it;
611: 
612:     // Format argument.
613:     visit_format_arg(ArgFormatter(out, specs, *this), arg);
614:   }
615:   return std::copy(start, it, out);
616: }

part.text:
Fixed. The bug was in `printf_arg_formatter::operator()` for `char_type` at include/fmt/printf.h:264, which unconditionally reset `fmt_specs.align = align::right`, discarding the left alignment set by the `-` flag in `parse_flags`. It now preserves `align::left` when set:

```cpp
if (fmt_specs.align != align::left) fmt_specs.align = align::right;
```

Verified: `printf-test` passes all 43 tests (including `MinusFlag` with `%-5c` → `"a    "`), and `format-test`, `core-test`, `format-impl-test`, `ostream-test` all pass.
